title: Regional clock drift caused quota desynchronization and cascading 429s — post-incident hardening
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Summary:
During a customer traffic surge on 2026-02-13 (18:07 UTC), our API gateway started returning a sustained stream of 429s from ~18:10–18:40 UTC in three regions. Total affected tokens: ~1.8M; estimated customer impact: medium (several high-traffic tenants experienced degraded user journeys and one partner integration fell back to cached responses).

What happened (concise):
- A configuration rollout shortened the quota lease window from 60s->20s to reduce perceived quota latency.
- Independently, a minor NTP glitch produced ~150–300ms clock skew on a subset of auth/enforcer nodes in us-west-2 and eu-central-1.
- The combination caused desynchronized lease renewals and overlapping quota accounting across the distributed enforcer ring: some tokens were double-counted while others were prematurely recharged.
- Our adaptive backoff logic reacted to increased failures by opening a conservative enforcement mode, which then amplified 429s (a feedback loop).

Root cause analysis:
- Primary root cause: timing assumptions in the quota enforcer algorithm (lease window treated as absolute across nodes) made the system sensitive to small cross-node clock drift.
- Contributing causes:
  1) Rolling config change that reduced lease window without staged rollout or canary across regions.
  2) Lack of health signals tied to clock synchronization in node scoring and routing decisions.
  3) No automatic graceful-degradation policy for enforcement during cross-region inconsistencies (we immediately switched enforcement mode instead of gradual throttling).
  4) Observability gap: our quota mismatch alert triggers on token delta > 5% after 10m; this was too slow to catch a 20–30 minute surge pattern.

Immediate mitigations applied (timeline):
- 18:12 UTC: Scoped rollback of the lease-window change (configuration reverted on control plane).
- 18:18 UTC: Emergency switch to best-effort enforcement mode for affected regions to allow in-flight requests to complete (reduced 429s).
- 18:25 UTC: Deployed a hotfix to backpressure logic to prevent enforcement mode flip-flops; added a 2-minute cooldown.
- 18:40 UTC: All regions stable; monitoring confirmed 429 rate returned to baseline by 19:05 UTC.

Action items and owners (short-term, planned):
1) Make quota lease window relative/clock-agnostic: change lease logic to use leader-clock or monotonic counters instead of node-local wall clock. Owner: @Marta Rodriguez. Due: 2026-03-15.
2) Add Clock-Sync health check into node scoring and routing (fail open on degraded NTP but mark node for rolling restart). Owner: @Connor Liu. Due: 2026-03-01.
3) Implement staged rollout guardrails for enforcement-critical config: require cross-region canary + pause toggle. Owner: @Priya Menon (SRE). Due: 2026-03-08.
4) Improve alerting: add a short-window quota-delta alert (1m/5m) and a chaos-detection signal for enforcement flap. Owner: @Data & Observability. Due: 2026-03-05.
5) Backpressure policy redesign: replace on/off enforcement flip with a smooth degradation curve and per-tenant emergency quotas. Owner: @Marta Rodriguez + @Alex Kim. Due: 2026-04-01.
6) Postmortem write-up and customer communication draft for affected tenants. Owner: @Ethan Brooks. Due: 2026-02-20 (completed).

Longer-term recommendations:
- Rework distributed quota protocol to use vector clocks or a centralized lease oracle for short windows where strict consistency matters.
- Run synthetic cross-region clock-drift tests in canary pipeline.
- Add a monthly audit for any config changes touching enforcement semantics.

Related artifacts and links:
- Dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/gateway/429s/2026-02-13
- Incident timeline doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood/platform/gateway/ENG-41005-incident-timeline
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/7891
- Rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/342

Notes on customer impact and follow-through:
- Primary affected customers were flagged and individual follow-up is in progress. Engineering will add per-tenant incident notes in the customer tracker.
- Legal and CS have been notified; draft external communication is awaiting approval (see attachments).
